rationale: Last sourced lead of the run, and it is a conditional one rather than a claim: the deprecated peer encoding that a protocol-1 leader uses for membership changes can only carry voters, so a configuration containing non-voters would lose them when written through that path. The question is registered paused with a discriminator, because reachability depends on whether a protocol-1 node can be leader while its configuration still carries non-voter or staging entries - a state the captured code does not obviously prevent but that this turn did not establish.

investigations.question: Can a membership change silently drop non-voter or staging servers when it is written through the deprecated peer encoding, i.e. when the leader runs a protocol version below 2 while its configuration contains entries of those suffrages?
investigations.hypothesis: A leader with protocolVersion below 2 encodes every membership change with the deprecated peer list, whose encoder gathers only voters and states that other suffrage types are not supported by the format; the decoder on the receiving side reconstructs voters only as well. A configuration that contained a non-voter or staging server would therefore be written back without it, and because nextConfiguration computed the full configuration (and only requires at least one voter), nothing on that path would report the loss.
investigations.discriminator: Establish whether a node with protocolVersion below 2 can be leader while configurations.latest contains a non-voter or staging entry: those entries can only enter through the versioned configuration format or through a snapshot, so the interesting cases are a deliberate downgrade of a running member, a mixed-version cluster where the older node wins an election, and a snapshot restored from a newer member. If such a state is reachable, a harness can drive one membership change on that leader and compare the entry's decoded configuration with the configuration the change requested; if the state is unreachable, or if the leader refuses or is replaced before appending, the concern is refuted. A defect requires a delivered entry whose decoded configuration is missing a server that the requested configuration contained.
resume_conditions: Resume when source or execution shows whether a protocol-version-below-2 leader can hold a configuration with non-voter or staging entries, for example after a downgrade, in a mixed-version cluster, or after restoring a snapshot written by a newer member.
Resume with a harness that appends one membership change on such a leader and decodes the appended entry, once reachability is established either way.

knowledge.statement: When the leader's protocol version is below 2, every membership change is appended as the deprecated remove-peer entry carrying encodePeers output, and encodePeers gathers only servers whose suffrage is Voter, with the comment that other suffrage types are not supported by that format; the matching decoder reconstructs a configuration of voters only, and the same encoder is also used to fill the peers field of a vote response for protocol-version-below-2 servers. The versioned configuration format is used for protocol version 2 and above.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to appendConfigurationEntry on a leader with protocolVersion below 2 and to decodePeers wherever a deprecated entry is processed; the lossy property only matters if the computed configuration contains a non-voter or staging server, which the deprecated format cannot represent.

interpretations.rationale: The lossy encoding is established from source; its reachability is not. appendConfigurationEntry chooses the entry format from the leader's protocol version alone: below 2 it appends a deprecated remove-peer entry whose payload is encodePeers(configuration) (raft.go:1219-1233), and encodePeers iterates the configuration taking only servers with suffrage Voter, with the stated reason that other suffrage types are not supported by the data format (configuration.go:311-327). The receiving side is symmetric: the deprecated entry is decoded with decodePeers, which reconstructs every server as a voter (configuration.go:330-352), and the same encoder fills the peers field returned to protocol-version-below-2 voters (raft.go:1620-1622). nextConfiguration had computed the full configuration and checkConfiguration only requires at least one voter, so a non-voter or staging entry in the computed configuration would not stop the append - it would simply not be representable in the written entry. What that means depends entirely on whether the precondition is reachable, and this turn did not establish it: non-voter and staging entries enter only through the versioned configuration format or through a snapshot from a member that used it, so the candidate paths are a deliberate downgrade of a running member, a mixed-version cluster in which the older node becomes leader, and a snapshot restored from a newer member (the version bounds themselves allow protocol 0 and above, config.go:100-106, with the handler accepting one version back). Until one of those is shown to produce a below-2 leader holding such a configuration, this stays a sourced boundary rather than a defect; the decisive test is to append one membership change on such a leader and compare the decoded entry with the configuration the change requested.
counterevidence: A cluster that has only ever run protocol 1 cannot have non-voter or staging entries in its configuration, because the deprecated format cannot introduce them; the concern is confined to downgrade, mixed-version and snapshot-restore states.

checkConfiguration still guarantees at least one voter, so the lossy path cannot produce a configuration with no voters - the risk would be losing non-voting members in the written entry, not losing the quorum.
limitations: No execution: no entry was appended or decoded, and no downgrade or mixed-version cluster was constructed.
